cohort: Pregnant women who delivered at a tertiary maternity hospital in London between September 1 and December 17, 2024, with the vaccine uptake analysis focused on those eligible for vaccination (n=911).
finding: RSV vaccine uptake increased significantly over time but showed disparities by ethnicity and socioeconomic status, with vaccinated women having a significantly lower rate of preterm birth <34 weeks.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were significantly higher among vaccinated women (52.0%) compared to unvaccinated women (35.5%).
cross-section timing: Data collected on deliveries between September 1 and December 17, 2024.
gest_age: For vaccine uptake analysis: delivered beyond 28 weeks' gestation and at 36 weeks or less on September 1, 2024. Outcomes included preterm birth <37 weeks and <34 weeks.
